config.title: Build websocket auth handshake

intro.title: Build websocket auth handshake
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a secure WebSocket authentication handshake for a Node.js server. You will learn how to verify a user's identity before allowing a WebSocket connection to be established. The core programming concept involves using HTTP headers to pass authentication tokens and validating them in a WebSocket upgrade request. You will work with the 'ws' library for WebSocket connections and Node.js HTTP modules to handle the handshake process. By the end, you'll have a server that only accepts connections from authenticated clients.
intro.usecase: WebSocket authentication handshakes are essential for securing real-time applications like collaborative document editors (Google Docs), live chat systems (Slack), and multiplayer gaming dashboards. When a user opens a trading platform dashboard or joins a video conferencing UI, this handshake validates their credentials before establishing the persistent connection. Developers implement this pattern to ensure only authorized users can access real-time data streams and interactive features, preventing unauthorized data exposure in financial, healthcare, or enterprise applications.

objectives: Implement a WebSocket server using the ws library in Node.js
Configure the server to handle connection upgrade requests
Initialize authentication token validation during the handshake phase
Construct proper HTTP response headers for successful and failed authentication
Manipulate WebSocket connections based on authentication status
Integrate token parsing logic with the connection upgrade handler
Control connection flow by rejecting unauthenticated clients

steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the http, WebSocket, and url modules from Node.js using the require() function.
steps.hint: Use require('module_name') for each module. These are built-in Node.js modules, so no npm installation is needed.
steps.expectedOutcome: The http, WebSocket, and url modules are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: The code imports http, WebSocket, and url modules using require().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import all three modules: http, WebSocket, and url.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use require() to import the http, WebSocket, and url modules from Node.js.

steps.title: Create HTTP server and WebSocket server
steps.instruction: Create an HTTP server using the http module and attach a WebSocket server to it using the ws module.
steps.hint: Use http.createServer() to create the HTTP server, then pass it to new WebSocket.Server({ server }) to attach the WebSocket server.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an HTTP server and WebSocket server set up, ready to handle connections.
successCriteria: An HTTP server is created with http.createServer() and a WebSocket server is attached to it with new WebSocket.Server({ server }).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both the HTTP server and WebSocket server are properly created and connected.
steps.feedbackWrong: create an HTTP server first, then attach a WebSocket server to it.

steps.title: Initialize authentication data storage
steps.instruction: Create an object to store valid authentication tokens in memory. Name it 'validTokens' and initialize it as an empty object.
steps.hint: You can create a simple JavaScript object using const validTokens = {};
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an in-memory store
const userSessions = {};
steps.expectedOutcome: An empty object named 'validTokens' is created to store authentication tokens.
successCriteria: The code contains a 'validTokens' variable initialized as an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a variable named 'validTokens' and initialized it as an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The authentication token storage wasn't created correctly. Please create an object named 'validTokens' to store tokens.

steps.title: Define authentication token validation function
steps.instruction: Create a function named `validateToken` that takes a token parameter and returns true if the token exists in the `validTokens` store, otherwise returns false.
steps.hint: You can use the `has` method on the `validTokens` Set to check if a token exists.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named `validateToken` is defined that checks if a provided token exists in the `validTokens` Set.
successCriteria: The `validateToken` function is defined, takes a token parameter, and returns a boolean based on whether the token exists in the `validTokens` Set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is named `validateToken`, takes a token parameter, and returns true/false based on whether the token exists in `validTokens`.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation function isn't quite right. You need to create a function named `validateToken` that checks if a token exists in the `validTokens` Set and returns a boolean value.

steps.title: Set up WebSocket connection handler
steps.instruction: Add an event listener to the WebSocket server to handle new connections. Use the 'connection' event and provide a callback function that takes a WebSocket client object as its parameter.
steps.hint: Use the wsServer.on('connection', ...) method. The callback function should accept one parameter (often named 'ws' or 'client') representing the new WebSocket connection.
steps.expectedOutcome: The WebSocket server will now detect when clients connect, but won't authenticate them yet.
successCriteria: The WebSocket server has a 'connection' event listener with a callback function that accepts a WebSocket client parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the 'connection' event listener to the WebSocket server with a proper callback function that accepts the client parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The connection handler isn't set up correctly. Remember to use wsServer.on('connection', callback) where the callback accepts the WebSocket client as a parameter.

steps.title: Parse URL query parameters
steps.instruction: Inside the WebSocket connection event listener, parse the incoming request URL to extract query parameters.
steps.hint: Use the URL module to parse the request URL and access its query parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: The WebSocket connection handler will be able to access authentication tokens from the URL query string.
successCriteria: The connection handler includes code to parse the request URL and extract query parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the URL module to parse the request URL and access the query object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The code doesn't yet parse the URL query parameters. Try using the URL module to parse the request URL.

steps.title: Extract authentication token from query
steps.instruction: Inside the WebSocket connection handler, extract the 'token' parameter from the parsed URL query object and store it in a variable.
steps.hint: Use the query object's properties to access the token value. For example, if the query object is stored in a variable called 'query', you can get the token with query.token.
steps.expectedOutcome: The token value from the URL query parameters will be accessible in a variable for validation.
successCriteria: A variable is declared that contains the 'token' value from the query object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're accessing the 'token' property from the query object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The token extraction isn't quite right. Check that you're getting the token value from the query object.

steps.title: Handle successful authentication
steps.instruction: Inside the connection handler, after validating the token, add logic to handle incoming messages from authenticated clients.
steps.hint: Use ws.on('message', ...) to listen for messages from the authenticated WebSocket connection.
steps.expectedOutcome: The WebSocket server will now process messages from authenticated clients.
successCriteria: The connection handler includes ws.on('message', ...) inside the successful authentication block.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure to add ws.on('message', ...) inside the successful authentication block.
steps.feedbackWrong: The message handling logic should be added inside the successful authentication block.

steps.title: Start the server and test
steps.instruction: Make the HTTP server listen on port 8080 and log a startup message to the console.
steps.hint: Use the server.listen() method with the port number and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will start and be ready to accept WebSocket connections with authentication.
successCriteria: The server is configured to listen on port 8080 with a console log message indicating it's running.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling server.listen() with port 8080 and a callback that logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't properly started. Check that you're using server.listen() with the correct port and logging a startup message.
